articles.title: Man sieht einen Feuerball, eine Rauchwolke. Der Roboter fährt einfach weiter
articles.teaser: Überall in der Ukraine laufen Fabriken auf Hochtouren, um Zehntausende neue Bodenroboter zu bauen. Die Fahrzeuge liefern Nachschub an die Front, bringen verletzte Soldaten zurück und haben laut Kiew bereits russische Stellungen einnehmen können. Doch sie haben eine Schwachstelle.
articles.image_title: Ukraines fight against the Russian invasion of its territory is almost about to enter its fifth year - with hundreds of thousands of lives lost in brutal warfare. The latest technological innovations from the Ukrainian side aim to fight the war remotely - by deploying robotic tank-style vehicles that can fight alongside infantry on the front line. A Ukrainian defence technology firm, DevDroid, says it intends to develop an unmanned ground combat system fitted with a 30mm cannon  a level of firepower that would mark a significant escalation in the role of combat robots in the war. DevDroids chief executive, Yurii Poritskyi, told Ukrainian defence outlet Militarnyi that the system is expected to operate effectively at ranges of up to four to five kilometres. That would place it well beyond the capabilities of earlier generations of Ukrainian ground robots, which have largely been used for reconnaissance, logistics and limited strike missions. Formal development of the new platform is due to begin in 2026, starting with detailed technical specifications. But Poritskyi acknowledged that mounting a 30mm cannon on a robotic vehicle presents major engineering challenges. The key issue is recoil, he said, noting that a cannon of this calibre generates far greater force than the lighter weapons previously fitted to robots. DevDroid envisages the future robot as both an assault system and a frontline support platform, operating alongside infantry units. Its role would include providing direct fire during attacks and helping to protect troops in high-threat environments where human soldiers are most at risk. If realised, analysts say the project would be among the most ambitious examples yet of Ukraines rapid shift towards unmanned ground systems  moving decisively from support roles towards heavily armed combat platforms. articles.title: Der Mann, der aus Frankreichs seltsamer Niederlage die tödliche Konsequenz zog
articles.teaser: Marc Bloch war Widerstandskämpfer und Historiker. Dafür wird er jetzt posthum in das Panthéon, die Ruhmeshalle Frankreichs, aufgenommen. Präsident Macron verfolgt damit eine eigene Agenda. „Nachfahren der Waffen-SS“ sind bei der Feier unerwünscht.
articles.image_title: A portrait of Marc Bloch, French historian and Resistance fighter, and his wife Simone Bloch is seen in Paris, France, on June 22, 2026. Bloch, born in Lyon on July 6, 1886, was executed by the Gestapo at Saint-Didier-de-Formans on June 16, 1944, and is set to be inducted into the Pantheon in Paris on June 23, 2026. (Photo by Adnan Farzat/NurPhoto)

articles.title: Diese Kreuzfahrerburg ist bis heute militärisch wertvoll
articles.teaser: Mindestens seit dem Hochmittelalter thront die Festung Beaufort im Südlibanon über dem Fluss Litani. Errichtet von den Kreuzfahrern, war sie seit 1268 in muslimischer Hand. Einer der berühmtesten Araber-Freunde Europas besuchte und beschrieb sie 1909.

articles.image_title: New Hungarian Prime Minister, Peter Magyar and Polish Prime Minister, Donald Tusk seen during their meeting at the Polish Prime Minister`s residence. On the morning of Wednesday, the 20th of May, on his first foreign visit, the new Prime Minister of Hungary, Peter Magyar, meets with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk. The visit symbolically marks the opening of a new phase in Budapest's relations with Europe. During the meeting the Prime Ministers discuss Magyar's victory in the recent Hungarian elections, the Polish-Hungarian relationship, and the issue of Zbigniew Ziobra and Marcin Romanowski - two Polish politicians evading prosecution in Poland by hiding in Hungary. After the meeting, Peter Magyar meets with the Polish President, Karol Nawrocki. (Photo by Neil Milton / SOPA Images/Sipa USA)
